title: Roads in Berland
statementMd:
There are $*n*$ cities numbered from 1 to $*n*$ in Berland. Some of them are connected by two-way roads. Each road has its own length — an integer number from 1 to 1000. It is known that from each city it is possible to get to any other city by existing roads. Also for each pair of cities it is known the shortest distance between them. Berland Government plans to build $*k*$ new roads. For each of the planned road it is known its length, and what cities it will connect. To control the correctness of the construction of new roads, after the opening of another road Berland government wants to check the sum of the shortest distances between all pairs of cities. Help them — for a given matrix of shortest distances on the old roads and plans of all new roads, find out how the sum of the shortest distances between all pairs of cities changes after construction of each road.

## Input

The first line contains integer $*n*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 300$) — amount of cities in Berland. Then there follow $*n*$ lines with $*n*$ integer numbers each — the matrix of shortest distances. $*j*$-th integer in the $*i*$-th row — $*d*_{*i*, *j*}$, the shortest distance between cities $*i*$ and $*j*$. It is guaranteed that $*d*_{*i*, *i*} = 0, *d*_{*i*, *j*} = *d*_{*j*, *i*}$, and a given matrix is a matrix of shortest distances for some set of two-way roads with integer lengths from 1 to 1000, such that from each city it is possible to get to any other city using these roads.

Next line contains integer $*k*$ ($1 ≤ *k* ≤ 300$) — amount of planned roads. Following $*k*$ lines contain the description of the planned roads. Each road is described by three space-separated integers $*a*_{*i*}$, $*b*_{*i*}$, $*c*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*} ≤ *n*, *a*_{*i*} ≠ *b*_{*i*}, 1 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ 1000$) — $*a*_{*i*}$ and $*b*_{*i*}$ — pair of cities, which the road connects, $*c*_{*i*}$ — the length of the road. It can be several roads between a pair of cities, but no road connects the city with itself.

## Output

Output $*k*$ space-separated integers $*q*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *i* ≤ *k*$). $*q*_{*i*}$ should be equal to the sum of shortest distances between all pairs of cities after the construction of roads with indexes from 1 to $*i*$. Roads are numbered from 1 in the input order. Each pair of cities should be taken into account in the sum exactly once, i. e. we count unordered pairs.
statementZhMd:
伯兰有 $*n*$ 座城市，编号为 1 到 $*n*$。其中一些城市由双向道路连接。每条道路都有自己的长度——一个介于 1 和 1000 之间的整数。已知从每座城市都可以通过现有道路到达其他任意城市。此外，对于每一对城市，还已知它们之间的最短距离。

伯兰政府计划修建 $*k*$ 条新道路。对于每条计划修建的道路，都已知其长度以及它将连接的两座城市。为了检查新道路建设的正确性，每修建完成一条道路后，伯兰政府都希望计算所有城市对之间最短距离之和。请帮助他们：给定旧道路的最短距离矩阵以及所有新道路的建设计划，求出每修建一条道路后，所有城市对之间最短距离之和的变化情况。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 300$）——伯兰的城市数量。接下来 $*n*$ 行，每行包含 $*n*$ 个整数——最短距离矩阵。第 $*i*$ 行的第 $*j*$ 个整数为 $*d*_{*i*, *j*}$，表示城市 $*i*$ 和城市 $*j*$ 之间的最短距离。保证 $*d*_{*i*, *i*} = 0, *d*_{*i*, *j*} = *d*_{*j*, *i*}$，并且给定矩阵是某组双向道路的最短距离矩阵。这些道路的长度为 1 到 1000 之间的整数，且从每座城市都可以通过这些道路到达其他任意城市。

下一行包含一个整数 $*k*$（$1 ≤ *k* ≤ 300$）——计划修建的道路数量。接下来的 $*k*$ 行描述计划修建的道路。每条道路由三个以空格分隔的整数 $*a*_{*i*}$、$*b*_{*i*}$、$*c*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$，$*a*_{*i*} ≠ *b*_{*i*}$，$1 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ 1000$）描述：$*a*_{*i*}$ 和 $*b*_{*i*}$ 是该道路连接的城市对，$*c*_{*i*}$ 是道路长度。两座城市之间可能有多条道路，但不会有道路连接城市与其自身。

## 输出格式

输出 $*k*$ 个以空格分隔的整数 $*q*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *i* ≤ *k*$）。$*q*_{*i*}$ 应等于修建编号从 1 到 $*i*$ 的道路后，所有城市对之间最短距离之和。道路按照输入顺序从 1 开始编号。每对城市在总和中恰好计算一次，即统计无序城市对。
